en.title: God’s Love Meets You
reflection: God’s love meets you exactly where you are, not where you think you should be. For many new believers, this is hard to accept. You may feel like you need to clean yourself up first, fix habits, or prove that you’re serious before God fully accepts you. But the message of Jesus starts in the opposite direction, God moves toward you first.

You might carry things from your past that still feel heavy: mistakes, regrets, patterns you’re not proud of, or even beliefs about God that make Him feel distant or strict. Maybe you’re coming from another religion where God felt far away, or maybe you never believed at all. Now you’re here, and part of you wonders: Does God really accept me like this?

The answer is yes. Not because your life is perfect, but because Jesus made a way for you to be received as you are. That doesn’t mean you stay the same, but it does mean you don’t start with earning his love. You start with receiving it.

You may not feel different right away. That’s normal. But something has already begun. The fact that you’re even open to God, thinking about Him, wanting to understand Him, that’s not random. That’s God drawing you in.
Learning to rest in that love takes time. You’ll revisit this truth again and again: God is not waiting to reject you, He’s already reaching for you.
en.activity: Write honestly to God about where you are right now, your doubts, your hopes, your past. Don’t filter it.

en.title: Trusting Jesus in Daily Life
reflection: Trusting Jesus is not a one-time decision; it’s a daily process. You may have already made a step of faith, but now comes the real question: what does it actually look like to trust Him in everyday life?

It’s easy to think that following Jesus means having everything figured out. But in reality, most of your growth will happen in ordinary moments. Decisions at work. Conversations at home. How you respond when you’re stressed, tired, or frustrated.
You might still rely on your old ways of thinking. That’s natural. Trust grows slowly. It develops as you begin to involve God in things you normally handle on your own.

Maybe it starts small: pausing before reacting, asking for guidance before a decision, or simply becoming aware that God is present with you in that moment. These small shifts matter more than big emotional experiences.
You don’t need perfect faith—you need practiced faith. And over time, as you continue to trust Him in small things, you’ll begin to see that He is trustworthy in bigger things too.
en.activity: Identify one area today where you usually act on autopilot. Pause and consciously invite God into it.

en.title: Peace Despite Mistakes
reflection: One of the biggest surprises in the Christian life is this: you will still mess up. Many new believers expect that once they follow Jesus, everything will change instantly. But then reality hits, you lose your temper, fall back into an old habit, or say something you regret.
And the question comes quickly: Did I just ruin everything? You didn’t.

Your relationship with God is not built on your ability to be perfect, it’s built on what Jesus has already done. That means when you fail, your response changes. Instead of hiding from God, you return to Him. Instead of pretending, you become honest.

Growth includes failure. But failure no longer defines you. In fact, these moments often become the places where your faith deepens the most. You begin to understand grace not just as an idea, but as something you experience. You learn humility. You learn dependence. You learn that God is patient.
Peace doesn’t come from getting everything right. It comes from knowing that even when you don’t, you are still held by God.
en.activity: Think about a recent mistake. Instead of avoiding it, talk to God about it honestly and receive His forgiveness.

en.title: God’s Spirit Is With You
reflection: You are not figuring this out alone. One of the most important truths for a new believer to understand is that God doesn’t just guide you from a distance, He is present with you through His Spirit.

At first, this can feel abstract. You might not know what it means to be “led by the Spirit.” You might expect something dramatic, like a strong voice or clear signs. But most of the time, His guidance is quieter. It can show up as a sense to pause before speaking. A feeling that something isn’t right. A nudge to reach out to someone. A growing awareness of what honors God and what doesn’t. You’re learning to recognize a new kind of guidance. And like any relationship, it takes time. You may ignore it sometimes. You may miss it. That’s part of the process. But over time, you begin to notice patterns. You become more sensitive. And slowly, you realize you’re not alone in your decisions anymore.
en.activity: Sit quietly for 5 minutes today and ask: “God, what do You want me to notice?”

en.title: Talking to God Honestly
reflection: Prayer is not about saying the right words—it’s about being real.

You may feel unsure how to pray. Maybe you’ve heard others pray and felt like you don’t measure up. Maybe you think you need to sound spiritual or formal. But Jesus teaches something very different. God is not impressed by performance, He desires honesty. That means you can come to Him with everything: confusion, frustration, gratitude, doubt, even silence. You don’t need to clean up your thoughts before bringing them.
Prayer is simply relationship.

At first, it may feel awkward. You may not know what to say. That’s okay. Start simple. Speak as you would to someone you trust. Over time, your confidence will grow, not because you learned a formula, but because you experienced connection. And something powerful happens when you begin to pray honestly: your perspective starts to change. You become less reactive, more grounded, more aware of God’s presence in your life.
en.activity: Spend 5 minutes talking to God out loud or in writing, no structure, just honesty.

en.title: Worship in Everyday Life
reflection: Worship is more than music, it’s how you live.

You might associate worship with singing in church, but in reality, worship is any response that recognizes God’s worth. That means your everyday life can become an act of worship. The way you work. The way you treat people. The way you respond when things don’t go your way. These all reflect what you value most.
As a new believer, learning to see life this way changes everything. Ordinary moments become meaningful. Small decisions become intentional. You begin to ask: Does this reflect who God is?

Worship shifts your focus. Instead of living centered on yourself, you begin to live with awareness of God. And that awareness brings gratitude, even in difficult moments. It doesn’t mean life becomes easy. But it does mean life becomes purposeful.
en.activity: Pause three times today and consciously thank God for something in that moment.

en.title: Peace in Anxiety
reflection: Following Jesus doesn’t remove anxiety, but it gives you a way to face it.

You may still feel worry, stress, or fear. That doesn’t mean your faith is weak. It means you’re human. The difference now is that you don’t have to carry those thoughts alone. God invites you to bring them to Him, honestly and regularly. This is not a one-time action. It’s a practice. You bring your concerns again and again. And over time, something shifts. Your problems may not disappear, but your perspective begins to change. You become less overwhelmed. More grounded. More aware that you are not alone in what you’re facing.
Peace is not the absence of difficulty. It’s the presence of God in the middle of it. And that peace grows as you learn to trust Him with what you cannot control.
en.activity: Write down what’s currently worrying you. Then pray through each point slowly, handing it to God.

en.title: Your Past Is Not Your Identity
reflection: One of the hardest things to truly believe as a new Christian is that your past no longer defines you. You may understand it intellectually, “I’m a new creation”, but emotionally, it often doesn’t feel true yet. You still remember who you were. The mistakes you made. The habits you struggled with. The things you regret. And sometimes those memories don’t just stay in the past, they follow you into the present, shaping how you see yourself. You might think: I’m still that person. I haven’t really changed. But God speaks something deeper than your feelings: you are new.

This doesn’t mean your personality disappears or your struggles instantly vanish. It means your identity has shifted. You are no longer defined by your worst moments, you are defined by what Jesus has done for you. Transformation rarely feels dramatic in the beginning. It’s often quiet. Subtle. You might notice small things first: a hesitation before doing something wrong, a desire to respond differently, a growing awareness of God. That’s real change.
God doesn’t erase your past, He redeems it. The very things you regret can become the places where you understand others better, where you show compassion, where your story becomes meaningful.
You are not starting from scratch—you are being rebuilt. And that takes time.
en.activity: Write down one part of your past that still feels heavy. Then write: “This no longer defines me, God is redeeming it.” Pray over it.

en.title: Will God Forgive Me Again?
reflection: At some point, every new believer asks this question: “What happens when I mess up again?”

Maybe you’ve already experienced it. You were serious about your faith, you wanted to change, and then you slipped. You said something you regret, returned to an old habit, or reacted in a way that doesn’t reflect who you want to be anymore. And immediately, the thought comes: Did I just undo everything? This is where understanding God’s forgiveness becomes critical.

God’s forgiveness is not fragile. It doesn’t depend on how well you perform after becoming a Christian. It is rooted in Jesus, not in your consistency. When you confess your sin, you are not restarting your relationship with God, you are restoring closeness within it. The relationship is still there. You are still His. That doesn’t mean sin doesn’t matter. It does. But it no longer separates you from God in the same way it once did. Instead, it becomes something you bring into the light, not hide in the dark.

Over time, something begins to change. You don’t just fear sin, you begin to see it differently. You desire something better. Your heart shifts. And that’s where real transformation happens. You are not disqualified when you fail. You are invited to come back, again and again.
en.activity: Think of a recent failure. Confess it honestly to God, then say out loud: “I am forgiven because of Jesus.”

en.title: Learning to Love Difficult People
reflection: Loving people sounds simple, until you actually try to do it.
It’s easy to love people who are kind, understanding, and easy to be around. But what about the ones who frustrate you? The ones who misunderstand you? The ones who push your patience to the edge?

As a new believer, this is where your faith becomes real. Jesus doesn’t call you to love selectively. He calls you to love as He has loved you. That means with patience, grace, and intentionality, even when it’s not deserved. This doesn’t mean ignoring boundaries or accepting harmful behavior. Loving someone does not mean allowing them to hurt you. But it does mean refusing to let bitterness take root in your heart. You may struggle with anger, irritation, or even resentment. That’s normal. Love is not the absence of those feelings, it’s the decision to respond differently despite them. Sometimes love looks like listening instead of reacting. Sometimes it looks like choosing not to escalate. Sometimes it simply means staying kind when it would be easier not to be. These small choices shape you. And over time, they reflect something powerful: a heart that is being changed by God.
en.activity: Think of one person you find difficult. Write one practical way you can respond differently to them this week.

en.title: Honoring in Difficult Relationships
reflection: Honoring others becomes complicated when relationships are not easy.

You may come from a family where there is tension, misunderstanding, or even past hurt. You may struggle with authority figures, parents, or people who simply don’t treat you well. So what does it mean to honor in those situations?
It doesn’t mean pretending everything is okay. It doesn’t mean agreeing with everything someone does. And it certainly doesn’t mean allowing yourself to be mistreated.

Honor is about how you carry yourself, not how others behave. It looks like choosing respect over contempt. It looks like controlling your words instead of reacting impulsively. It looks like refusing to let someone else’s behavior determine your character. This is not easy. In fact, it may be one of the most challenging areas of growth for you. But it’s also one of the most powerful. Because when you choose honor in difficult situations, you break patterns. You step out of cycles of reaction and into intentional living. And that reflects God’s character in a very real way.
en.activity: Identify one relationship where you struggle. Write down one way you can respond with honor instead of reaction.

en.title: Trusting God in Everyday Decisions
reflection: Faith is not just about big life decisions, it’s built in the small ones you make every day.

You might think trusting God means major choices: career, relationships, big turning points. But most of your growth will happen in ordinary, everyday decisions. How you respond when you’re tired. How you speak when you’re frustrated. How you handle pressure, temptation, or opportunity. These moments seem small—but they shape your life.

Trusting God in these situations means slowing down enough to ask: What honors Him here? You won’t always get it right. Sometimes you’ll react too quickly. Sometimes you’ll fall back into old patterns. But each time you pause and invite God into the moment, you strengthen your awareness of Him. And over time, that awareness becomes more natural. You begin to think differently. Respond differently. Choose differently. Not because you’re forcing it, but because your heart is changing.
en.activity: Before making one decision today, pause and ask: “God, guide me.” Then follow through.

en.title: When Temptation Feels Strong
reflection: Temptation doesn’t disappear when you become a Christian. In fact, sometimes it feels stronger because now you’re more aware of it. You may find yourself drawn back to old habits, things you thought you had left behind. And when that happens, it can feel discouraging. You might think: Why am I still struggling with this? But temptation is not failure. It’s part of the process.

The key difference now is that you are no longer powerless. God promises that there is always a way out. It may not feel obvious in the moment, but it is there. Sometimes it looks like walking away. Sometimes it looks like changing your environment. Sometimes it means reaching out to someone or redirecting your thoughts.

Victory doesn’t always feel dramatic. Often, it looks like quiet decisions, choosing not to act on something you used to give in to. And those decisions matter. Each time you resist, even in small ways, you grow stronger. And over time, what once controlled you begins to lose its grip.
en.activity: Identify your most common temptation. Write down one practical step you can take to respond differently next time.

en.title: You Were Not Meant to Do This Alone
reflection: One of the biggest mistakes new believers make is trying to grow alone.
You might think your faith is something private, something you figure out on your own. But the Christian life was never meant to be lived in isolation.
You need people. Not perfect people, but real people who are also trying to follow Jesus. People who can encourage you, challenge you, pray with you, and walk alongside you.

At first, this can feel uncomfortable. Especially if you’re not used to opening up or trusting others. You might feel unsure where you fit or whether you belong. That’s normal. But community doesn’t start deep, it starts small. A conversation. A connection. A shared moment. Over time, those small steps build something stronger. And in that space, your faith grows in ways it never could on its own. Because sometimes, you need someone else to remind you of what is true when you forget.
en.activity: Reach out to one believer this week. Start a simple conversation about faith, no pressure, just connection.

en.title: People Notice Change
reflection: When your life begins to change, people will notice, even before you fully understand what’s happening yourself. Maybe your reactions are softer, your words more careful, or your priorities shifting. You may not feel radically different, but others will pick up on it.

This can create tension. Some people may ask questions. Others may joke about it. Some might even feel uncomfortable around you. And that can make you second-guess yourself: Am I being too different? Should I tone it down? But here’s the truth, your role is not to manage other people’s reactions. Your role is to be faithful.

Jesus calls you the light of the world. Light doesn’t argue its presence, it simply shines. It reveals what’s real. And sometimes, that makes people uncomfortable because it exposes contrast. You don’t need to preach to everyone. You don’t need to correct everyone. What matters most is consistency. When your life aligns with your faith—how you treat people, how you respond under pressure, how you handle conflict, that speaks louder than words ever could.

Over time, people who are genuinely curious will ask. And when they do, you’ll be ready, not because you have all the answers, but because you’ve lived something real. There may also be moments where you feel misunderstood or even isolated. That’s part of following Jesus. But you are not alone in that. God sees your faithfulness in the small, unseen moments. And those moments matter more than you think.
en.activity: Write down two changes you’ve noticed in yourself. Then write one sentence explaining your faith in simple words.

en.title: Sharing Your Faith Naturally
reflection: Sharing your faith can feel intimidating, especially if you feel like you don’t know enough yet. You might think you need to have all the answers, or be able to defend every question someone throws at you.

But that’s not what God asks of you. What people need most is not a perfect explanation, they need authenticity. Think about it: no one can argue with your experience. They might question your beliefs, but they can’t deny what’s changed in your life.

Maybe you’ve found peace where there used to be anxiety. Maybe you’ve become more patient. Maybe you’re thinking differently about people, about yourself, about purpose. That matters. Sharing your faith doesn’t have to be a formal moment. It can happen in normal conversations. It can sound like: “Honestly, I’ve just been trying to follow Jesus more lately, and it’s changing how I see things.”

It’s simple. It’s real. Also, your tone matters. You’re not trying to win an argument, you’re trying to reflect Christ. That means humility, respect, and listening well. Some people will be open. Some won’t. That’s not your responsibility. Your responsibility is to be faithful and honest. And remember, you’re not alone in these conversations. God is at work in ways you can’t see.
en.activity: Write your story in 4–5 sentences: what your life was like, what changed, and what it means now.

en.title: Do I Need New Friends?
reflection: This is one of the most real and sometimes uncomfortable questions: “Do I need to change my friends?”

The answer is not simply yes or no, it’s wisdom. You don’t need to cut people out of your life just because they don’t share your faith. In fact, maintaining those relationships can be meaningful and even impactful. But you do need to recognize influence.

Ask yourself honestly: Who pulls me toward the person I’m becoming? And who pulls me back toward the person I used to be? That doesn’t mean labeling people as “good” or “bad.” It means being aware of how your environment shapes you. If certain relationships consistently lead you into old habits, compromise, or confusion, that’s something to take seriously.

At the same time, you may feel a sense of loss as your priorities change. Some friendships might feel different. Conversations might not connect the same way. That can feel lonely. But God is not removing people to leave you empty, He is guiding you toward relationships that strengthen your faith.
This is not about isolation. It’s about alignment. You can still love people deeply without letting every influence shape your life.
en.activity: Write down your 5 closest influences. Next to each, write: “builds me” or “pulls me back.” Pray for wisdom.

en.title: When You Feel Lonely
reflection: Loneliness is something many new believers don’t expect, but it’s very real.

As your life begins to change, you may feel like you don’t fully fit where you used to, and you’re not yet fully connected where you’re going. That in-between space can feel heavy. You might sit in a room full of people and still feel alone. You might scroll through your phone and feel disconnected. You might wish someone understood what’s happening inside you.

Here’s what matters: God is not distant in your loneliness. In fact, some of the deepest growth in your faith will happen in these quiet, uncomfortable spaces. When external support feels limited, your dependence on God grows stronger. But that doesn’t mean you’re meant to stay isolated. Loneliness is not just something to endure, it’s something to respond to. God often invites you to take small, intentional steps toward connection. Send a message. Join a group. Start a conversation. Even if it feels awkward. Growth often begins with uncomfortable steps. And over time, those steps lead to real community.
en.activity: Spend 10 minutes with God in silence. Then message one person just to connect, no pressure, just a step.

en.title: Building a Prayer Rhythm
reflection: One of the most important habits you will build is prayer, but consistency is often the hardest part.

You might start strong, then get distracted. Life fills up. Your mind gets busy. And suddenly, prayer becomes occasional instead of daily. That’s normal, but it’s also where growth can stall. Jesus regularly withdrew to pray. Not because He had to, but because He chose to stay connected to the Father.

Prayer is not about saying the right words. It’s about staying in relationship. Think of it like this: short, consistent moments with God are more powerful than occasional long ones. A few minutes in the morning. A pause in the middle of your day. A reflection at night. These rhythms anchor your life. You may not always feel something dramatic, and that’s okay. Faith grows quietly, through consistency.
Don’t aim for perfect—aim for present.
en.activity: Set two specific times today (morning and evening) to pause and pray for 3–5 minutes.

en.title: Understanding Scripture
reflection: Reading the Bible can feel confusing at first, and that’s completely normal.

You might not understand everything. You might wonder what certain passages mean or how they apply to your life. Don’t let that discourage you. The goal is not instant understanding, it’s consistent exposure. Over time, as you read, patterns begin to form. You start recognizing God’s character. You begin to understand His ways. Your thinking slowly changes. Even one verse can shape your day if you take it seriously.

Also remember, you’re not reading just for information. You’re reading for transformation. Ask simple questions: What does this show me about God? What does this mean for how I live? Growth happens when you engage, not just read. And over time, what once felt confusing becomes familiar.
en.activity: Read today’s passage slowly. Write down one truth and one way it applies to your life.

en.title: Living With Integrity
reflection: Integrity is one of the clearest signs of real faith, but it’s often tested in private.

It shows up in moments where no one is watching. When you have a choice between what’s easy and what’s right. When you could cut corners, stay silent, or justify something, but choose not to. As a new believer, these moments may feel small, but they are shaping you.

Integrity is not about perfection. It’s about alignment. Choosing to live in a way that reflects what you believe, even when it costs you something. Over time, this builds strength in your character. It also builds trust—with others, and within yourself.

You begin to live with less internal conflict, because your actions and your faith are moving in the same direction. God is deeply concerned with who you are becoming, not just what you say you believe.
And integrity is where that becomes visible.
en.activity: Identify one situation today where you can choose integrity over convenience. Act on it.

en.title: Growth Takes Time
reflection: It’s easy to feel like you should be further along by now. You might look at others who seem more mature in their faith and wonder why you’re still struggling in certain areas.

But spiritual growth is not instant, it’s a process. God is not measuring you against others. He is working in you personally, shaping you over time. Every prayer matters. Every small decision matters. Every moment you choose to trust Him instead of yourself matters. Even when you don’t feel progress, something is happening beneath the surface. Just like roots grow before anything is visible above ground, your faith is being established in ways you may not yet see.
You are not behind. You are being formed. And God is faithful to complete what He started in you.
en.activity: Write down three ways you’ve changed or grown since starting this journey.

en.title: Serving Others
reflection: Faith becomes real when it moves outward. It’s easy to focus inward, your growth, your struggles, your questions. But one of the fastest ways to grow is to begin serving others.

Serving shifts your perspective. You begin to notice people more. You become aware of needs around you. And you start to reflect the heart of Jesus in practical ways. You don’t need a big opportunity. It can be something simple like helping someone, encouraging them, listening when they need it. What matters is the posture of your heart. And here’s the surprising part: when you serve others, you grow.
Your faith becomes active. It becomes visible. It becomes real. And over time, serving shapes you into someone who naturally reflects Christ.
en.activity: Do one intentional act of service today. Keep it simple but do it with purpose.

en.title: Humility Changes Everything
reflection: Pride can quietly slow your growth without you realizing it. It shows up in defensiveness, comparison, or the need to always be right.

Humility, on the other hand, creates space for growth. When you admit you need God, you open yourself to His help. When you listen instead of react, you gain understanding. When you choose to learn instead of defend, you grow. Humility is not weakness, it’s strength that is grounded and secure. It allows God to work more deeply in your life because you are no longer resisting Him. And over time, humility transforms how you relate to others as well. You become more patient, more understanding, more grounded.
Growth accelerates where humility is present.
en.activity: Reflect on one situation where you reacted defensively. Write how you could respond differently next time.

en.title: Letting God Carry You
reflection: Life can feel heavy, even as a believer. Responsibilities, expectations, stress, and pressure don’t disappear when you come to faith.

You might still feel overwhelmed at times. You might still try to carry everything yourself. But God invites you into a different way of living. He doesn’t ask you to ignore responsibility, but He does ask you not to carry it alone. When you bring your burdens to Him, something shifts. You gain perspective. You gain strength. You begin to experience peace even in the middle of pressure. God may not remove every difficulty, but He strengthens you within it. And over time, you learn to rely on Him more naturally. You stop trying to control everything, and start trusting more deeply.
en.activity: Write down what is currently weighing on you. Pray through each item slowly.

en.title: Bringing Hope to Others
reflection: Your life now carries something valuable - hope. Not because everything is perfect, but because God is present and active in you.

People around you may be dealing with things you don’t see, stress, anxiety, discouragement, or pain. And sometimes, a simple word, a kind action, or your presence can bring light into those situations. You don’t need to fix anyone. You don’t need to have perfect answers. You just need to be available.

Hope is often shared in quiet ways, a conversation, a message, a moment of encouragement. And when you bring hope to others, it strengthens your own faith as well. You begin to see that God is not only working in you, but through you.
en.activity: Encourage one person today with a sincere and thoughtful message.

en.title: Facing Pushback
reflection: At some point, your faith will be tested socially. Someone may question you, challenge you, or not understand your decisions.

This can feel uncomfortable, especially if it comes from people you care about. You may feel the pressure to explain everything perfectly, or to defend yourself strongly. But that’s not always necessary. Your role is not to win every conversation, it’s to remain grounded. Respond with calm. Respond with respect. Respond with clarity when needed, but don’t let pressure push you into reacting out of fear or frustration. Over time, your consistency will speak louder than your arguments.
And even if people don’t agree with you, they will notice how you carry yourself. That matters.
en.activity: Think of a situation where you might face pushback. Write down a calm and respectful response.

en.title: Joy in Obedience
reflection: Obedience can feel restrictive at first, but it leads to freedom. You may feel like you’re giving things up or limiting yourself.

But over time, something shifts. You begin to see that God’s direction is not about control, it’s about life. His ways lead to peace, clarity, and joy that doesn’t depend on circumstances. Obedience is not about following rules, it’s about trusting a relationship. And as that trust grows, obedience becomes less of a struggle and more of a desire. You begin to want what God wants.
And that’s where real joy begins.
en.activity: Identify one area where you know what’s right. Take one step of obedience today.

en.title: Living as Light
reflection: Your life now reflects something greater than yourself. Every decision, every reaction, every word carries influence.

You don’t need to be perfect to reflect Christ, you need to be intentional. Living as light means choosing what is good, right, and true, even when it’s not easy. It means being aware that your life is now visible in a different way. People are watching, not to judge you, but to understand what faith looks like in real life. And through your consistency, they begin to see something different.
Not perfection, but authenticity. And that is powerful.
en.activity: Identify one situation today where you can intentionally reflect Christ through your actions.

en.title: Keep Going
reflection: This is just the beginning of your journey. These 30 days are not the finish line, they are a foundation.

There will be days where you feel strong in your faith. There will be days where you struggle, doubt, or feel distant. That’s normal. What matters most is consistency. Keep showing up. Keep praying. Keep reading. Keep trusting.

Faith is not about never falling, it’s about continuing to move forward. God is not waiting for you to be perfect. He is walking with you as you grow. And He will continue to shape you, guide you, and strengthen you over time. Stay committed to the journey. Because the journey is where transformation happens.
en.activity: Write down one habit you will continue after these 30 days, and commit to it.

en.name: New Believer Devotional
closing: Keep walking. Keep growing. God is not finished with you.
You’ve begun something meaningful. Keep walking with God daily, He is faithful!
